name: Select private funds and commit capital
summary: The fund investments team decides which private equity funds to back and commits capital to them, mostly re-ups with general partners it already knows plus a few new managers each year. A case starts when a fund comes to market, passes a pipeline screen, goes through track record analysis, review of the ILPA questionnaire, meetings, references and operational due diligence, and becomes a memo that Risk reviews and the Portfolio Execution Committee approves. Legal then negotiates the side letter, operations completes subscription and know-your-client forms, and the commitment is live when the general partner accepts it at a closing. Elapsed time is driven by waits on general partners, committee calendars, rounds of side letter markups and the general partner's closing dates, while popular funds compress the diligence window.

baseline.org_archetype: A national public pension investment manager of about 2,000 staff whose private equity department commits C$100 million to C$1 billion per fund to about 160 managers, with in-house legal and investment operations.
baseline.notes: Described as commonly run at large Canadian pension investors in the period, with email, a deal pipeline system, data rooms and spreadsheets.

trigger: A general partner launches a fund raise (a re-up for an existing manager or an offering from a new one) and the team logs it for screening.
end_state: The commitment is accepted at a closing and set up in the private admin system, or the opportunity is declined at screen, operational due diligence or committee.

volume.seasonality: Fund launches cluster after Labour Day and in the first quarter; commitments bunch before general partners' final closes.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file's 5 to 12 cases a month. Cases are opportunities taken to the pipeline meeting; with the decline rates in the graph about 6 a month (about 70 a year) end in commitment, consistent with about 168 PE fund relationships (131 in Funds and Secondaries, 37 in Asia) on four- to five-year fund cycles plus a few new managers and some real asset and credit funds.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Document management and investment committee memo repository
General partner and fund administrator investor portals
Virtual data rooms run by sellers and advisors
Private investments administration and cash flow system
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse

steps.name: Log fund offering in pipeline
steps.description: A funds team analyst records a new fund raise in the deal pipeline system when a general partner or placement agent sends a private placement memorandum, or when the monitoring team flags that an existing manager is coming back to market. The analyst saves the memorandum and fundraising timetable in the document store and requests data room access.

error.defect_description: Wrong target close date or fund size typed into the pipeline record.

evidence.note: NC policy: each viable opportunity and contact is logged in an opportunity database as offering memoranda arrive.

steps.name: Screen the offering against the mandate
steps.description: An associate reads the memorandum and the summary track record, checks the strategy, fund size and timing against the department mandate and annual commitment pacing, and looks up prior fund results and monitoring notes for an existing manager. The associate writes a one-page screening note recommending whether to spend diligence time on the fund.

error.defect_description: Pacing or concentration fit misjudged because monitoring data were stale.

evidence.note: NC policy Phase III preliminary fund screen: fit with work plan, history with the firm, prior fund performance, terms and closing timing.

steps.name: Decide at weekly pipeline meeting
steps.description: The group head chairs the weekly funds pipeline meeting, hears the screening notes and decides which offerings get full diligence, given team capacity, the target close date and the commitment budget. Offerings that do not fit are declined and the general partner is told.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Department mandate and annual commitment pacing approved through the business plan

evidence.note: Weekly pipeline meeting and 20% decline at this stage are estimates; NC policy describes screening at regular internal staff meetings. Most offerings reaching this point are re-ups with existing managers, which are rarely declined at screen.

steps.name: Request DDQ, track record and data room
steps.description: The associate asks the general partner for its completed ILPA due diligence questionnaire, deal-level cash flows for prior funds, the draft limited partnership agreement, team biographies and reference contacts. For a re-up the request is limited to an updated questionnaire and the latest deal data.

error.defect_description: Request omits items needed later, such as the fund administrator's controls report.

evidence.note: ILPA DDQ 2.0 with appendices for requested documents, references, team and portfolio templates.

steps.name: Wait for GP questionnaire and data
steps.description: The general partner's investor relations team uploads the questionnaire answers, track record files and draft fund documents to its data room. Responses for large funds are often staged, with sensitive items given later or only in meetings.

error.defect_description: Incomplete or inconsistent track record data from the GP.

evidence.note: ILPA user guide: GPs may provide sensitive answers in person, redacted or later in diligence. Wait duration is an estimate.

steps.name: Analyse track record and portfolio
steps.description: An analyst loads the deal-level cash flows into the team's spreadsheet model and calculates gross and net IRR, multiples, realised and unrealised splits, loss ratios, dispersion by deal partner and a public market equivalent against a listed index. The analyst compares results with peer benchmark quartiles and flags deals whose marks look high.

error.defect_description: Formula or cash flow mapping error in the track record model.

evidence.note: NC policy: quantitative analysis of performance, fees and incentives; ILPA DDQ track record section. Hours are estimates.

steps.name: Review strategy, team and terms
steps.description: A senior associate reads the questionnaire answers and draft agreement, checks key person, GP commitment, fee, carried interest and expense terms against ILPA Principles and the department's preferred terms, and lists open questions. The senior associate decides with the principal whether a full onsite review is needed.

error.defect_description: A non-standard term in the draft agreement is missed.

next.condition: new manager or material change: full onsite review

evidence.note: Terms reviewed against ILPA Principles 3.0; NC policy requires assessment of willingness to accept preferred terms. The 40% share of cases needing onsite work is an estimate from the small number of new managers added each year (PE Asia added three in F2021).

steps.name: Hold GP meetings and onsite visit
steps.description: The principal and senior associate meet the general partner's investment team at its offices, interview partners one by one, review recent deals and value creation work, and test the strategy against the track record findings. Travel and calendars of both sides set the timing.

error.defect_description: Meeting notes miss a team departure risk.

evidence.note: NC policy: manager presentations and onsite visits to the manager's offices. Hours and waits are estimates.

steps.name: Make reference calls
steps.description: The principal calls references the general partner listed and others found independently, such as former portfolio company executives, co-investors and other limited partners, and writes up what each said about the team, conduct and alignment.

error.defect_description: References are only those chosen by the GP and give a one-sided view.

evidence.note: NC policy: reference checks with other investors, limited partners, consultants and industry contacts; ILPA DDQ appendix C reference template.

steps.name: Get internal reference from Credit Investments
steps.description: A Credit Investments principal who has lent to the general partner's portfolio companies, or a colleague who co-invested with the manager, gives a short internal view on how the sponsor behaves in negotiations and when deals go wrong. The view is noted for the memo.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: The fund's partners generated C$41.7 billion of direct invested capital since inception, so other teams usually know the sponsor; the internal call itself is an estimate.

steps.name: Run operational due diligence
steps.description: A funds operations senior associate reviews the operations sections of the questionnaire, the fund administrator, auditor, valuation policy, controls report, cash and wire controls and cybersecurity, and holds a call with the general partner's chief financial officer. The reviewer rates the manager as pass, pass with follow-up items, or fail.

error.defect_description: Weak cash controls at the GP not identified.

control.basis: Investment Operations operational due diligence standard for external managers

evidence.note: Cambridge Associates ODD review areas; NC policy requires risk and operational due diligence reviews to accompany the memo. Pass and fail rates are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for GP answers to operational follow-ups
steps.description: The general partner's finance team answers follow-up questions, for example on who can release wires, how valuations are approved or which administrator will be used, and sends supporting policies.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate of GP turnaround on operational follow-up questions.

steps.name: Send term sheet to Tax
steps.description: The associate sends Tax a short term sheet with the fund's legal structure, jurisdictions, expected investments and proposed commitment so Tax can choose the holding entity and check withholding and filing exposure. The tax structure memo comes back while the memo is being drafted.

error.defect_description: Fund structure misdescribed, causing a later change of investing entity.

evidence.note: ILPA DDQ asks the GP for the fund's legal and tax structure chart; the handoff to Tax follows the organisation's process map.

steps.name: Review LPA and list side letter requests
steps.description: Legal counsel reads the draft limited partnership agreement against the organisation's standard positions and ILPA Principles and drafts the side letter requests a Crown corporation investor needs, such as preserved immunities, tax status, confidentiality, reporting and most favoured nation rights. Counsel writes a key legal issues summary for the memo.

error.defect_description: An LPA provision that conflicts with the investor's tax status is missed.

control.basis: Legal review of fund documents required before commitment under Management Authorities

evidence.note: Cooley lists the side letter provisions public pension and governmental investors request; ILPA Principles set LP positions on terms.

steps.name: Draft commitment memo
steps.description: The senior associate writes the investment memo: thesis, team, strategy, track record, terms and fees, operational due diligence result, tax structure, legal issues, portfolio fit, commitment size and risks. Exhibits come from the track record model and the issues lists.

error.defect_description: Numbers in the memo do not match the model, or a risk is understated.

evidence.note: NC policy lists memo content (SWOT, GP background, returns, merits and risks, operational assessment, terms). Wait includes time for the tax structure memo. Hours are estimates.

steps.name: Review and edit memo
steps.description: The director who leads the funds team reads the memo with the principal, checks the numbers against the model, challenges the thesis and sizing, and sends it back with comments or clears it for the group head.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Rework rate of one in four is an estimate from typical investment committee memo practice.

steps.name: Sponsor memo and submit to Risk and PEC
steps.description: The group head reads the memo, confirms it fits the department's Investment Management Authority and pacing, and submits it to the Portfolio Execution Committee agenda and to Risk for an independent opinion.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Management Authorities: commitments are approved by the Portfolio Execution Committee on a sponsor's recommendation

evidence.note: F2022 annual report: PEC reviews new investments for approval and checks alignment with the strategy's mandate.

steps.name: Answer Risk questions
steps.description: Risk reviews the memo for concentration, liquidity and leverage effects on the total fund and sends questions. The senior associate answers them, updates exhibits and waits for the written risk opinion that goes to the committee.

error.defect_description: Updated exhibit not carried into the committee version of the memo.

control.basis: Independent risk opinion on investment proposals (second line of defence)

evidence.note: The F2022 report describes a three lines of defence model and Risk oversight; the questions and turnaround are estimates.

steps.name: Present at PEC and receive decision
steps.description: The group head and principal present the commitment at the Portfolio Execution Committee chaired by the Chief Investment Officer and answer questions. The committee approves, asks for more work, or declines.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Portfolio Execution Committee approval under the Board-approved authorities policy

evidence.note: PEC chaired by the CIO reviews new investments for approval. Meeting frequency and approval rates are estimates.

steps.name: Negotiate side letter and final terms
steps.description: Legal counsel sends the side letter and LPA comments to the general partner's counsel, negotiates fee breaks for commitment size, reporting, confidentiality and tax provisions, and agrees which points rely on the most favoured nation clause. The deal team joins calls on economic points.

error.defect_description: Side letter commitment amount or entity name differs from the subscription documents.

evidence.note: Cooley primer on side letter provisions and MFN; F2021 report notes negotiation of better aligned terms with fund managers.

steps.name: Wait for GP counsel response
steps.description: The general partner's counsel reviews the requests against what other investors were given and returns a markup, often holding back points until it has seen all side letters for the closing.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: ILPA Principles note side letter negotiation and compliance costs can be sizeable; turnaround and number of rounds are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare subscription, KYC and tax forms
steps.description: A funds operations senior associate completes the subscription agreement and investor questionnaire, assembles the know-your-client package (constating documents, incumbency and signing authority, beneficial ownership statement for a Crown corporation) and the US or other tax forms, and sets the notice contacts and bank instructions for capital calls.

error.defect_description: Missing or out-of-date KYC item, wrong investing entity or unsigned tax form.

evidence.note: Cooley: side letters and tax forms are part of the closing process; ILPA released a model subscription agreement to streamline subscriptions. Hours are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm execution versions
steps.description: Legal counsel checks that the final LPA, side letter and subscription agreement match the approved terms, the commitment amount and the investing entity named in the tax memo, then releases them for signature.

error.defect_description: A late GP change to the LPA slips through.

control.basis: Legal sign-off on execution versions before signature

evidence.note: Practice estimate; mismatches between side letter and subscription amounts are a known source of rework.

steps.name: Sign under authorised signatories
steps.description: Two authorised officers, normally the group head and a second senior signatory, sign the subscription agreement and side letter electronically after checking the approval record.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Two authorised signatories required under the signing authority policy within Management Authorities

evidence.note: Formalised Management Authorities are described in the F2022 report; the two-signature rule is an assumption.

steps.name: Wait for GP and administrator review
steps.description: The general partner's fund administrator checks the subscription package for anti-money-laundering and tax completeness and either confirms it or asks for missing items such as a certified register or a newer incumbency certificate.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Most managers use third-party administrators who run investor onboarding checks; the 25% return rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Wait for closing and GP acceptance
steps.description: The commitment is accepted when the general partner holds its next closing and countersigns, which may be weeks away because closings are batched. Investors in later closings may owe an equalisation payment.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: ILPA Principles: fundraising should end within about 12 months of the initial close and later investors pay interest; spacing of closings is an estimate.

steps.name: Set up commitment in private admin system
steps.description: A funds operations senior associate creates the fund, commitment, fee terms and side letter obligations in the private investments administration system, records the verified notice and bank details for future calls, files the executed documents and tells the monitoring team and Finance the commitment is live.

error.defect_description: Commitment amount, fee terms or currency keyed wrongly, later caught when the first capital call is checked.

control.basis: Four-eyes check of new commitment static data under internal control over financial reporting

evidence.note: Set-up task inferred from the organisation's private admin system and capital call controls; hours are estimates.

exceptions.name: Re-up without onsite review
exceptions.description: For an existing manager with an unchanged team and strategy the team skips the onsite visit and outside references and relies on monitoring knowledge and an update call.

exceptions.name: Operational follow-up loop
exceptions.description: Operational due diligence finds gaps (for example a single person able to release wires or no independent administrator) and waits for the GP's fixes before passing.

exceptions.name: Committee sends memo back
exceptions.description: The committee asks for more analysis, such as a different commitment size or more on a key person risk, and the memo returns to drafting.

exceptions.name: Missing KYC or tax items
exceptions.description: The GP's administrator rejects the subscription package for a missing or stale document and operations re-sends it.

exceptions.name: Declined after diligence
exceptions.description: The manager fails operational due diligence or the committee declines, after weeks of team effort.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from logging the offering to the commitment being accepted and set up
benchmarks.population: Large sophisticated public pension LPs committing to private equity funds, re-ups and new managers combined

evidence.note: Estimate. PEI reported in 2014 that a quarter of investors need more than 12 months for a single fund commitment, but that covers all LP types and first contact; large in-house teams with re-up relationships move faster, and the GP's closing schedule adds weeks at the end.

benchmarks.population: The model fund private equity, F2021

evidence.note: Estimate: PE Asia added three new managers out of 37 relationships in F2021; most commitments are re-ups.

pain_points.description: Popular funds set short windows before final close, so diligence, memo and committee time are compressed and the team works to the GP's timetable.

evidence.note: ILPA Principles on fundraising periods; compression is a practitioner observation.

pain_points.description: Questionnaires and track record files arrive in different formats and need re-keying into the team's model, despite the ILPA DDQ.

evidence.note: ILPA says customised DDQs created an extraordinary administrative burden and outsized effort.

pain_points.description: Side letter negotiation runs in several rounds and depends on what the GP has given other investors, often pushing signing close to the closing date.

evidence.note: Cooley warns against negotiating side letters in the rush of closing; ILPA notes sizeable side letter costs.

pain_points.description: Subscription packages bounce for missing KYC or tax items, adding a week or more at the end.

evidence.note: Practitioner estimate.

assumptions: The process covers the full path from a fund coming to market to the commitment being accepted. The Portfolio Execution Committee's own deliberation is modelled in tf-pec-approval and the risk opinion in risk-transaction-review; steps s17 to s19 here hold only the funds team's time. Legal fund-document work is modelled here (s14, s20, s23) although the organisation file's lc-negotiate-close also lists fund documents; a combined model should count it once.
Signed subscription documents go to general partners through lc-negotiate-close in the organisation file's map, so they are not listed as an output here.
The tax structure memo is an input that arrives mid-process (before s15), not a case trigger, so its trigger share is 0.

Real Assets and Credit fund commitments follow the same flow with a Real Assets or Credit principal leading; ra_principal is not given separate steps. ci_principal appears only as an internal reference.

Cases are fund opportunities taken to the pipeline meeting (8 a month); about 75% end in a commitment. Commitments above the Board threshold would also go to the Board's Investment Strategy Committee; this is rare for fund commitments and not modelled.
Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file and include incentive pay, so labour cost per case is high.
Hands-on times, waits, decline and rework rates are tier C estimates unless a source is cited.
